cirneco-cons-ampd2-study-2024.name: Murgiano et al. (2024) - Frameshift Variant in AMPD2 in Cirneco dell'Etna Dogs with Retinopathy and Tremors (Genes)
cirneco-cons-ampd2-study-2024.note: Peer-reviewed study (Genes 2024;15(2):238, PMID: 38397227, PMCID: PMC10887799) identifying a 1-bp frameshift deletion in exon 15 of AMPD2 on CFA6 (g.42,698,170delC / c.2131delG / p.D711Mfs12Stop) associated with Cirneco oculo-neurological syndrome (CONS) in two male littermates and three related carriers.

nsdtr-immune-mediated-disease-patterns-2.name: Disease Patterns and Incidence of Immune-Mediated Disease in Insured Swedish Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers
nsdtr-immune-mediated-disease-patterns-2.note: Bremer HD, Vilson Å, Bonnett BN, Hansson-Hamlin H (Veterinary Record 2015;177(3):74). Epidemiological cohort study of 2,890 insured Swedish Tollers (2002–2007) reporting elevated relative risk and incidence rates for SRMA (20 per 10,000 DYAR; RR 12) and IMRD (6.8 per 10,000 DYAR; RR 18), higher lymphoma risk, and lower ear and heart disease rates compared with other breeds.

nsdtr-immune-mediated-health-survey-2024.name: In Sickness and Health - A Questionnaire-Based Study of Immune-Mediated Diseases and Neoplasia in Swedish Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers
nsdtr-immune-mediated-health-survey-2024.note: Nilsson K et al. / Hansson-Hamlin H (Acta Veterinaria Scandinavica 2024;66:39). Questionnaire study of 935 living and 177 deceased Swedish Tollers reporting living lifetime prevalence of 3.0% for IMRD and 3.5% for SRMA, owner-reported neoplasia of any type in 14% of living dogs (mammary 22%, mast cell 15%), and neoplasia as cause of death in 38.4% of deceased dogs.

nsdtr-resf1-jadd-study-2026.name: A Variant in RESF1 Is Associated with Addison's Disease and Multiple Autoimmune Syndrome in Young Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers
nsdtr-resf1-jadd-study-2026.note: Brown EA, Cullen JN et al. / Bannasch DL (Scientific Reports 2026;16:13194). Identifies an autosomal recessive missense variant in RESF1 (Chr27:29,736,795, c.3170C>T, p.Pro1057Leu) associated with juvenile-onset Addison's disease (~75% penetrance by 1 year, median onset 5 months) and multiple autoimmune syndrome (41.7%–70.8% concurrent immune disorders; median survival 2.0 years).

uc-davis-vgl-jadd-nsdtr.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Juvenile Addison's Disease in Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retrievers
uc-davis-vgl-jadd-nsdtr.note: UC Davis VGL test page for the RESF1 c.3170C>T (p.Pro1057Leu) juvenile Addison's disease (JADD) variant, documenting autosomal recessive inheritance with incomplete (~75.9%) penetrance, ~20%–23% carrier frequency, concurrent ocular/immunologic comorbidities, and breeding guidance.

hokkaido-association-of-north-america-ab.name: Hokkaido Association of North America - About Hokkaido
hokkaido-association-of-north-america-ab.note: National breed club overview covering temperament, appearance, coat colours, grooming, house manners, vocalization, pica, and potty training.

hokkaido-association-of-north-america-hi.name: Hokkaido Association of North America - Hokkaido History
hokkaido-association-of-north-america-hi.note: National breed club history covering Ainu origins, Thomas Blakiston (1869), the 1902 Hakkōda Mountains army rescue, the 1937 Natural Monument designation, DOKENHO (1954), and Otōsan.

hokkaido-association-of-north-america-he.name: Hokkaido Association of North America - Hokkaido Health
hokkaido-association-of-north-america-he.note: National breed club health statement detailing mandatory and optional pre-breeding clearances, Collie eye anomaly (CEA), heart murmurs, hip dysplasia, idiopathic seizures, anxiety, psychogenic polydipsia, and pica.

united-kennel-club-hokkaido-breed-standa.name: United Kennel Club - Hokkaido (Ainu) Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-hokkaido-breed-standa.note: Official UKC breed standard for the Hokkaido (recognized as Ainu in 1996, renamed Hokkaido in 2008; Northern Breed Group).

hokkaido-cea-nhej1-study.name: Veterinary Ophthalmology - Collie Eye Anomaly in Hokkaido Dogs: Case Study
hokkaido-cea-nhej1-study.note: Peer-reviewed study by Mizukami et al. (Vet Ophthalmol 2012;15(2):128-132; DOI: 10.1111/j.1463-5224.2011.00950.x) identifying the intronic 7.8-kb NHEJ1 deletion in Hokkaido dogs.

hokkaido-cea-mdr1-selection-study.name: Veterinary Record - Investigation of Parallel and Simultaneous Selection for Collie Eye Anomaly and Ivermectin Toxicosis
hokkaido-cea-mdr1-selection-study.note: Peer-reviewed study by Mizukami et al. (Vet Rec 2014;175(7):174; DOI: 10.1136/vr.102015) confirming a 0.667 mutant allele frequency for the NHEJ1 Collie eye anomaly deletion (12/18 carriers, 6/18 affected) and 0% frequency for the MDR1/ABCB1 defect in tested Hokkaido dogs.

fci-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore-stand.name: FCI - Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore Standard No. 322
fci-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore-stand.note: Official FCI English breed standard for Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore (Great Anglo-French Tricolour Hound, Standard No. 322, published 1996-06-18; official valid standard dated 1983-01-27).

fci-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore-nomen.name: FCI - Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore Breed Nomenclature (No. 322)
fci-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore-nomen.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry (No. 322) confirming definitive recognition on 1983-01-27, Group 6 Section 1.1 classification, working-trial requirement, and official multilingual breed names (Great Anglo-French Tricolour Hound, Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore, Großer Anglo-Französischer Dreifarbiger Laufhund, Gran Sabueso Anglo-Francés Tricolor).

venerie-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.name: Société de Vénerie - Races : Le Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore (Standard FCI N° 322)
venerie-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.note: Full French text of FCI Standard No. 322 (valid standard 27.01.1983) published by the Société de Vénerie, along with French pack-hound kennel, disease-prevention, and working guidance.

chien-com-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.name: Chien.com - Grand Anglo-Français Tricolore
chien-com-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.note: Secondary French breed profile noting Poitevin, Gascon Saintongeois, and English Foxhound ancestry and reporting secondary height (62–72 cm males, 60–68 cm females) and weight (29–30 kg) estimates.

wikimedia-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.name: Wikimedia Commons - File:Grand anglo francais tricol.jpg
wikimedia-grand-anglo-francais-tricolore.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for photograph by Alephalpha (captured 2006-10-22, uploaded 2008-10-21, 1200x800 px), dual-licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 and GFDL 1.2+.

wikimedia-largeanglofrench-tricolore1-ca.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for photograph by Canarian (captured 2022-04-24, uploaded 2022-04-27, 2045x1772 px), licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

italian-greyhound-club-of-america-about.name: Italian Greyhound Club of America - About the Italian Greyhound
italian-greyhound-club-of-america-about.note: National breed club guide covering temperament, exercise, grooming (daily tooth brushing, 1–3x weekly nail grinding), puppy/adult feeding schedules, house-training, and jump/fracture safety.

italian-greyhound-club-of-america-histor.name: Italian Greyhound Club of America - Italian Greyhound Breed History
italian-greyhound-club-of-america-histor.note: National breed club history covering ancient Mediterranean origins, Renaissance nobility and artists, royal owners, 1886 AKC registration, and post-WWII European repopulation.

italian-greyhound-club-of-america-health.name: Italian Greyhound Club of America - Italian Greyhound Health
italian-greyhound-club-of-america-health.note: Official IGCA Health Testing Recommendations (also published at https://www.akc.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Health-Statement-Italian-Greyhound-Club-of-America-2026-Final.pdf).

the-italian-greyhound-club-uk-breed-stan.name: The Italian Greyhound Club (UK) - Official Breed Standard
the-italian-greyhound-club-uk-breed-stan.note: Official UK breed standard under the auspices of The Kennel Club specifying ideal height 32–38 cm (12.5–15 in), ideal weight 3.6–4.5 kg (8–10 lbs), and accepted colours.

uc-davis-vgl-italian-greyhound-health-pa.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Italian Greyhound Health Panel (FEH, PCAG, PRA-IG1)
uc-davis-vgl-italian-greyhound-health-pa.note: UC Davis VGL documentation for FEH (https://vgl.ucdavis.edu/test/feh-ig), PCAG (https://vgl.ucdavis.edu/test/pcag-susceptibility-ig), and PRA-IG1 (https://vgl.ucdavis.edu/test/pra-susceptibility-ig).

italian-greyhound-feh-enam-study.name: Animal Genetics - Simple Recessive Mutation in ENAM Is Associated with Amelogenesis Imperfecta in Italian Greyhounds
italian-greyhound-feh-enam-study.note: Peer-reviewed study by Gandolfi et al. (Anim Genet 2013;44(5):569-578; DOI: 10.1111/age.12043) identifying the 5-bp deletion in exon 10 of ENAM causing familial enamel hypoplasia (14% affected, 30% carriers).

italian-greyhound-autoimmune-diversity-s.name: Canine Genetics and Epidemiology - A Search for Genetic Diversity Among Italian Greyhounds from Continental Europe and the USA and the Effect of Inbreeding on Susceptibility to Autoimmune Disease
italian-greyhound-autoimmune-diversity-s.note: Peer-reviewed study by Pedersen et al. (Canine Genet Epidemiol 2015;2:17; DOI: 10.1186/s40575-015-0030-9; PMID: 26526059) analyzing genetic bottlenecks, DLA class I/II homozygosity, and multiple autoimmune diseases in Italian Greyhounds.

fci-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-orange.name: FCI - Grand Anglo-Français Blanc et Orange Standard No. 324
fci-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-orange.note: Official FCI English breed standard for Grand Anglo-Français Blanc et Orange (Great Anglo-French White and Orange Hound, Standard No. 324; current official valid standard dated 2023-08-01, English publication 2023-10-06; original valid standard 1983-01-27).

fci-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-orange.name: FCI - Grand Anglo-Français Blanc et Orange Breed Nomenclature (No. 324)
fci-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-orange.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry (No. 324) confirming definitive recognition on 1983-01-27, Group 6 Section 1.1 classification, working-trial requirement, current valid standard date (2023-08-01), and official multilingual breed names (Great Anglo-French White & Orange Hound, Grand Anglo-Français Blanc & Orange, Großer Anglo-Französischer Weiß-Oranger Laufhund, Gran Sabueso Anglo-Francés Blanco y Naranja).

ukc-great-anglo-francais-white-and-orang.name: United Kennel Club - Great Anglo-Français White and Orange Hound Breed Standard
ukc-great-anglo-francais-white-and-orang.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognized in 2006, Scenthound Group) specifying complete scissors bite, black or orange-brown nose, 23.5–27.5 inch height at withers, coat and colour rules, and disqualifications (cryptorchidism, viciousness or extreme shyness, albinism).

worldlydogs-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-e.name: Worldly Dogs - Grand Anglo-Français Blanc et Orange
worldlydogs-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-e.note: Secondary breed overview consulted cautiously for historical context and traditional pack-hunting background.

wikimedia-grand-anglo-francais-blanc-et-.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for photograph by Alephalpha (captured 2006-10-22, uploaded 2008-10-23, 640x480 px), dual-licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 and GFDL 1.2+.

fci-tornjak-official-standard.name: FCI - Tornjak Official Breed Standard No. 355
fci-tornjak-official-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 355 (dated 2017-11-23; original valid standard published 2017-11-07) for the Tornjak (Bosnian and Herzegovinian – Croatian Shepherd Dog), covering origin, historical summary (1067 and 1374 records; 1972 recovery; 1978 purebred breeding), utilization, Group 2 Section 2.2 classification, temperament, conformation proportions (length exceeding height by no more than 8%, 1:1 skull-to-muzzle ratio, ~120° shoulder angle), coat, colour, height (males 65–70 cm, females 60–65 cm, ±2 cm tolerance), and disqualifying faults.

fci-tornjak-nomenclature.name: FCI - Tornjak Breed Nomenclature
fci-tornjak-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry No. 355 confirming multilingual breed names, origin in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia, Group 2 Section 2.2 (Molossian type, Mountain type) classification without working trial, provisional acceptance on 2007-06-01, and definitive acceptance on 2017-11-07.

american-kennel-club-tornjak.name: American Kennel Club - Tornjak Breed Profile
american-kennel-club-tornjak.note: Official AKC breed profile (recorded in the Foundation Stock Service since May 2012 with Working Group designation) providing height (23–28 inches), weight (62–110 pounds), life expectancy (12–14 years), historical registration under the name Kanis Montanus and etymology from 'tor' (livestock enclosure), temperament, grooming, exercise, training, and nutrition guidance.

ukc-tornjak-official-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Tornjak Breed Standard
ukc-tornjak-official-standard.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognized 2011-08-18; revised 2017-05-01) classifying the Tornjak in the Guardian Dog Group and specifying history, character, conformation, coat, colour, height (males 25.5–27.5 in, females 23.5–25.5 in, ±0.75 in tolerance), eliminating faults, and disqualifications.

tornjak-club-north-america-breed-profile.name: Tornjak Club of North America - About the Breed
tornjak-club-north-america-breed-profile.note: North American breed-club profile detailing the Tornjak's Balkan mountain origins, livestock-guardian temperament, average height (23–28 in), average weight (60–120 lbs), and lifespan (12–14 years).

tornjak-club-north-america-health-concer.name: Tornjak Club of North America - Health Concerns
tornjak-club-north-america-health-concer.note: Breed-club health guidance on gastric dilatation-volvulus (GDV / bloat, including resting after meals, feeding smaller frequent meals, and avoiding elevated food bowls) and hip and elbow dysplasia (pre-breeding joint screening, controlled puppy growth, and weight management).

tornjak-hip-dysplasia-monitoring-study-2.name: Results of Radiological Hip Dysplasia Monitoring in Tornjak Breed
tornjak-hip-dysplasia-monitoring-study-2.note: Peer-reviewed retrospective study (Vrbanac et al., Veterinarski arhiv 2022;92(5):599–607, DOI: 10.24099/vet.arhiv.1409) of 735 Tornjak hip radiographs evaluated from 2001 to 2016 (median age 18 months), finding 74.97% healthy (grades A/B) and 25.03% dysplastic (grades C/D/E) overall (76.86% healthy and 23.14% dysplastic in 523 dogs under 24 months) and a significant reduction in severe grade E hip dysplasia over the 15-year period.
tornjak-hip-dysplasia-monitoring-study-2.publisher: Faculty of Veterinary Medicine, University of Zagreb (Veterinarski arhiv)

tornjak-hip-dysplasia-biomarker-study-20.name: Breed-Specific Evaluation of Serum Biochemical Markers in Canine Hip Dysplasia Observed in a Tornjak Dog Population
tornjak-hip-dysplasia-biomarker-study-20.note: Peer-reviewed study (Alilovic et al., Am J Vet Res 2023;84(11):ajvr.23.07.0170, PMID: 37699541) evaluating serum hyaluronic acid (HA), procollagen II C-terminal propeptide (PIICP), and matrix metallopeptidase 9 (MMP9) activity across 99 adult Tornjaks in Bosnia and Herzegovina (51 non-dysplastic grades A/B vs. 48 dysplastic grades C/D/E).
tornjak-hip-dysplasia-biomarker-study-20.publisher: American Veterinary Medical Association (American Journal of Veterinary Research)

wikimedia-tornjak-and-puppy-tomasz-wasko.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Tornjak and puppy.jpg', photographed by Tomasz Waśko (uploader TomaszVasco) on 2023-05-20 and uploaded on 2023-05-26 under CC BY-SA 4.0 (4966 × 3311 px).

wikimedia-tornjak-female-canarian.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Bosnian and Herzegovinian - Croatian Shepherd Dog aka Tornjak.jpg', photographed by Canarian on 2008-10-31 and uploaded on 2013-01-20 under CC BY-SA 3.0 (495 × 408 px).

skg-schweizer-laufhund.name: Schweizer Laufhund — Rasseporträt (mit dem Schweizerischen Laufhundeclub SLC)
skg-schweizer-laufhund.note: Official Swiss Kennel Club breed portrait co-authored with the Schweizerischer Laufhundeclub (SLC), documenting height (47–59 cm), weight (18–23 kg), history, working styles, temperament, exercise, and health/ear care.

schweizerischer-laufhundeclub-zuchtregle.name: Zuchtreglement des Schweizerischen Laufhunde-Clubs (ZR-SLC-2021)
schweizerischer-laufhundeclub-zuchtregle.note: Official breeding regulations of the Swiss breed club (approved by the SKG Central Committee on 2021-04-28), covering mandatory breeding inspection (Ankörung) at 15+ months, minimum breeding age (18 months), and conformation/behavioural requirements.

united-kennel-club-swiss-hound-breed-sta.name: Swiss Hound — Official UKC Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-swiss-hound-breed-sta.note: Official UKC breed standard (Scenthound Group, recognized January 1, 2006), confirming height (19–23 in / 49–59 cm males, 18.5–22.5 in / 47–57 cm females), four varieties, and coat colours.

russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-standa.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Official AKC Breed Standard
russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-standa.publisher: Russian Toy Club of America (RTCA) / American Kennel Club (AKC)
russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-standa.note: Official AKC breed standard (approved July 14, 2017; effective June 27, 2018), specifying height (8–11 in; disqualifying <7 in or >12 in), weight (up to 6.5 lbs; disqualifying <2 lbs), coat length (1–3 in, full ear fringe after 3 years), and accepted colours.

russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-histor.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Breed History
russian-toy-club-of-america-breed-histor.note: Official parent-club history documenting the 1716–1725 preserved specimen at the Zoological Museum in St. Petersburg, the 1958 long-coated progenitor Chiki, the 1966 standard, and the 1988 unification of the two varieties.

russian-toy-club-of-america-faq.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
russian-toy-club-of-america-faq.note: Official parent-club FAQ covering appearance, coat colour eye/nose pigment rules, minimal shedding, puppy coat drop between 5 and 12 months, full coat/fringe maturation at 2–3 years, and harness safety.

russian-toy-club-of-america-health-and-g.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Health & Genetics Committee
russian-toy-club-of-america-health-and-g.note: Official RTCA Health & Genetics page listing core OFA screenings (Patellar Luxation, Ophthalmology Exam, Basic Cardiology Exam), optional OFA screenings (Legg-Calvé-Perthes, Hip Dysplasia, Elbow Dysplasia, Paired Serum Bile Acid), and Cornell Biobank sample collection for PRA and Legg-Calvé-Perthes.

russian-toy-club-of-america-performance.name: Russian Toy Club of America — Performance & Nose Work
russian-toy-club-of-america-performance.note: Official RTCA performance overview documenting participation in agility, obedience, rally, lure coursing, trick training, and nose work.

united-kennel-club-russkiy-toy-breed-sta.name: United Kennel Club — Russkiy Toy Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-russkiy-toy-breed-sta.note: Official UKC breed standard (recognized 2008, revised February 1, 2018; Companion Dog Group), specifying height 8–11 in (preferred 10 in), weight up to 6 lbs (preferred 5 lbs; eliminating fault <3 lbs or >6 lbs; disqualifying <2 lbs), and all 11 coat colours.

fci-bullmastiff-official-standard.name: FCI - Bullmastiff Official Breed Standard No. 157
fci-bullmastiff-official-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 157 (header dated 06.10.2026; official valid standard published 08.09.2026) covering Great Britain origin, Group 2 Section 2.1 classification without working trial, utilization, historical summary, temperament, head proportions (1:3 muzzle-to-head ratio, level/pincer or slightly undershot bite, non-pendulous flews), conformation, coat, colour (brindle, fawn, or red with essential black muzzle and slight white chest mark permissible), height (males 64–69 cm, females 61–66 cm), and weight (males 50–59 kg, females 41–50 kg).

american-kennel-club-bullmastiff.name: American Kennel Club - Bullmastiff
american-kennel-club-bullmastiff.note: Official AKC breed profile covering height (males 25–27 in, females 24–26 in; male average 26 in), weight (males 110–130 lbs, females 100–120 lbs; male average 120 lbs), life expectancy (7–9 years), 'The Gamekeeper's Night Dog' nickname, 1860 English origins, 1933/1934 AKC recognition, grooming, exercise, training, nutrition (several small puppy meals, two adult meals daily, post-meal rest), and recommended health tests (hip, elbow, cardiac, ophthalmologist, and thyroid evaluations).

royal-kennel-club-bullmastiff-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Bullmastiff Breed Standard
royal-kennel-club-bullmastiff-standard.note: Official UK breed standard (last updated 1 August 2025) specifying Working Group classification, conformation, temperament, coat, colour, height (dogs 64–69 cm / 25–27 in, bitches 61–66 cm / 24–26 in), and weight (dogs 50–59 kg / 110–130 lbs, bitches 41–50 kg / 90–110 lbs).

royal-kennel-club-bullmastiff-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Bullmastiff Breed Profile
royal-kennel-club-bullmastiff-profile.note: Official UK breed profile detailing 19th-century gamekeeper history, brindle nighttime camouflage, breed characteristics (large house, large garden, weekly grooming, under 10 years lifespan, >2 hours daily exercise listing), Breed Watch Category 2 status, short-muzzle/facial-fold care, and Good Practice pre-breeding schemes (elbow, eye, and hip testing).

american-bullmastiff-association-health-.name: American Bullmastiff Association - Health Statement
american-bullmastiff-association-health-.note: Official parent-club health statement recommending pre-breeding screening for hip dysplasia, elbow dysplasia, autoimmune thyroiditis / hypothyroidism, ophthalmic disorders, and cardiac disease.

american-bullmastiff-association-common-.name: American Bullmastiff Association - Common Diseases and Conditions
american-bullmastiff-association-common-.note: Parent-club health reference covering high pain tolerance, allergies, bloat (GDV), cancer (hemangiosarcoma, lymphoma/lymphosarcoma, mast cell tumors, osteosarcoma, mammary tumors), cardiac disorders (valvular murmurs, sub-aortic stenosis [SAS], cardiomyopathy), eye disorders (entropion, autosomal dominant PRA, retinal dysplasia), hypothyroidism, kidney/urinary disease (chronic renal failure, cystinuria, glomerulonephritis, renal amyloidosis, juvenile renal dysplasia), and orthopedic conditions (hip/elbow dysplasia, cruciate ligament rupture, HOD, OCD, and panosteitis).

petmd-bullmastiff-health-and-care.name: PetMD - Bullmastiff Dog Breed Health and Care
petmd-bullmastiff-health-and-care.note: Veterinary-authored breed guide (by Michelle Diener, DVM; reviewed by Molly Price, DVM; updated 15 April 2025) covering 7–9 year lifespan, dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM), subaortic valvular stenosis (SAS), entropion, progressive retinal atrophy (PRA), hip/elbow dysplasia, lymphoma, bloat/GDV and prophylactic gastropexy, feeding (2–3 meals/day at floor level, slow-feeder bowls, 1-hour rest before/after meals), moderate drooling and daily jowl wiping, allergy-related ear care, training, and fenced-yard/housing guidance.

merck-veterinary-manual-gastric-dilatati.name: Merck Veterinary Manual - Gastric Dilatation and Volvulus in Small Animals
merck-veterinary-manual-gastric-dilatati.note: Peer-reviewed veterinary reference (by Kevin P. Winkler, DVM, DACVS; reviewed August 2025) detailing GDV pathophysiology, risk factors, clinical signs, emergency stabilization and derotation, and preventive measures (multiple small meals, exercise restriction around meals, reducing mealtime stress, avoiding elevated bowls, and prophylactic gastropexy).

wikimedia-bullmastiff-desaix83.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Bullmastiff.jpg' (589 × 509 px, CC BY-SA 3.0), uploaded on 2015-03-17 by Desaix83 as a white-background derivative of 'File:Bullmastiff edited.JPG' (originally photographed by Fausto Moreno on 2006-10-07).

fci-bucovina-shepherd-dog-official-stand.name: FCI - Romanian Bucovina Shepherd Official Breed Standard No. 357
fci-bucovina-shepherd-dog-official-stand.note: Official FCI Standard No. 357 (valid standard dated 20 August 2023; English version published 1 September 2023) covering Romanian Carpathian/Bucovina transhumance origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 classification without working trial, utilization, temperament, head proportions (1:1 skull-to-muzzle ratio, 16–18 cm male / 15–17 cm female skull width, scissor or level bite), conformation, dark ash-grey skin, double coat (6–9 cm body hair, neck mane, limb fringes/culottes), classical pied and solid colours (brindle patches rejected), height (males 68–78 cm, ideal 71–75 cm; females 64–72 cm, ideal 66–68 cm; ±4 cm tolerance), weight in proportion to height, and faults/disqualifications.

fci-bucovina-shepherd-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Romanian Bucovina Shepherd Nomenclature No. 357
fci-bucovina-shepherd-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI breed nomenclature page for Ciobănesc Românesc de Bucovina (No. 357), confirming Romania origin, Group 2 Section 2.2 (Molossian type, Mountain type) classification without working trial, provisional acceptance on 2009-03-26, definitive acceptance on 2019-04-29, official valid standard date 2023-08-20, and multilingual standard publication on 2023-09-01.

uc-davis-canine-hip-dysplasia.name: UC Davis School of Veterinary Medicine - Canine Hip Dysplasia
uc-davis-canine-hip-dysplasia.publisher: University of California, Davis, School of Veterinary Medicine
uc-davis-canine-hip-dysplasia.note: Veterinary reference (by John Gardiner, 24 April 2019) covering multifactorial genetics of canine hip dysplasia, caloric intake and growth rate management, lean body condition, and pre-breeding radiographic evaluation.

avma-pet-dental-care.name: American Veterinary Medical Association - Pet Dental Care
avma-pet-dental-care.note: General veterinary guidance for routine dental prevention and veterinary oral checks.

wikimedia-bucovina-shepherd-canarian-201.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Bucovina Shepherd.jpg' (2343 × 1791 px, CC BY-SA 4.0), photographed by Canarian on 2019-09-07 (Sony DSLR-A350 EXIF) and uploaded on 2019-09-09.

american-kennel-club-boykin-spaniel-offi.name: American Kennel Club - Official Standard for the Boykin Spaniel

royal-kennel-club-hovawart-profile.name: The Royal Kennel Club — Hovawart Breed Profile
royal-kennel-club-hovawart-profile.note: UK kennel-club breed profile confirming Working Group placement, Breed Watch Category 1 status, 1936 German Kennel Club recognition, exercise guideline (>2 hours/day), grooming (>once/week), shedding, lifespan (>10 years), and Best Practice BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme screening.

hovawart-club-of-great-britain-breed-int.name: Hovawart Club of Great Britain — Breed Introduction
hovawart-club-of-great-britain-breed-int.note: UK breed-club introduction detailing Harz, Black Forest and Odenwald origins, Kurt König's post-WWI reconstruction, 1947 postwar club formation, 1980 UK arrival and 1982 UK club founding, all three colours occurring in a single litter, 2-year maturation, height (63–70 cm / 58–65 cm) and weight (30–40 kg / 25–35 kg).

hovawart-club-of-great-britain-health.name: Hovawart Club of Great Britain — Health & Breeding Code of Ethics
hovawart-club-of-great-britain-health.note: UK breed-club health page and Code of Ethics (Clauses 15.3–15.5) requiring pre-breeding hip scoring (maximum individual BVA score 20, maximum combined parent score 25; UK breed median 8–9), thyroid testing within 2 years of mating (Total T4, Free T4, cTSH, and TgAA; tested halfway between seasons in bitches and >=30–45 days post-vaccination), and Degenerative Myelopathy (SOD1) DNA testing to avoid producing homozygous DM/DM offspring, plus GDV/bloat awareness.

hovawart-club-of-great-britain-care.name: Hovawart Club of Great Britain — Care and Grooming
hovawart-club-of-great-britain-care.note: UK breed-club care guide covering long-pin slicker and rotating-tooth comb brushing, mat-prone zones (behind ears, elbow feathers, rear-leg feathering), optional ear/foot hair trimming to reduce grass seeds and mud, growth-spurt nutrition, controlled puppy exercise, scent work, and weekly puppy veterinary weighing visits.

hovawart-club-of-north-america-faq.name: Hovawart Club of North America — Frequently Asked Questions
hovawart-club-of-north-america-faq.note: North American parent-club FAQ covering suitability for first-time owners, space needs, defensive vs. aggressive guarding instincts, 10–14 year lifespan, <5% hip dysplasia rate, and HCNA breeding requirements (two Very Good/Excellent conformation ratings, temperament test at >=20 months, OFA Good or Excellent hips at >=24 months, annual eye exam, full thyroid panel, and Breeding Director approval for genetic diversity).

american-kennel-club-american-english-co.note: Official AKC breed profile; provides height (24–26 in male, 23–25 in female), weight (45–65 lbs), lifespan (11–12 years), coat and colour information, working history, temperament, grooming, nutrition, and health guidance.

american-kennel-club-american-english-co.name: Regulations for AKC Coonhound Bench Shows, Field Trials, Nite Hunts and Water Races — History and Official Standard for the American English Coonhound
american-kennel-club-american-english-co.note: AKC Coonhound Regulations (amended to October 2021) and History & Standards for Coonhound Breeds (Pages 60–63: American English Coonhound history and official standard, approved April 2009, effective 1 January 2010).

united-kennel-club-english-coonhound-sta.name: United Kennel Club — English Coonhound Official Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-english-coonhound-sta.note: Official UKC English Coonhound breed standard (revised 1 January 2016); documents 1905 registration as English Fox & Coonhound, 1945/1946 Walker and Bluetick separations, height limits (22–27 in males, 21–25 in females), permitted coat colours (including white and lemon), and disqualifications.

american-kennel-club-american-english-co.name: American Kennel Club — American English Coonhound History: Why Most Call Them 'English Dogs'
american-kennel-club-american-english-co.note: AKC breed-history feature by Denise Flaim (updated 16 February 2024) covering British foxhound ancestry, 'English dogs' terminology, 'barking up the wrong tree' origin, bear/cougar baying, 1920s Leafy Oak winner 'Bones', and ticking distinctions from the Bluetick and Treeing Walker Coonhounds.

akc-english-setter-profile.name: American Kennel Club — English Setter
akc-english-setter-profile.note: Breed profile covering measurements (males 25–27 in / 65–80 lb; females 23–25 in / 45–55 lb), 12-year life expectancy, care, grooming, exercise, nutrition, and recommended health tests.

english-setter-association-breed-standar.name: English Setter Association (UK) — Breed Standard
english-setter-association-breed-standar.note: Reproduces the UK Kennel Club breed standard (published August, amended November 2002); specifies height of 65–69 cm (25.5–27 in) for dogs and 61–65 cm (24–25.5 in) for bitches.

english-setter-association-health.name: English Setter Association (UK) — Health
english-setter-association-health.note: UK breed-club health overview covering hip dysplasia, atopic dermatitis, hypothyroidism, congenital deafness (BAER testing), and DNA testing for PRA-rcd4 and NCL.

pubmed-english-setter-congenital-deafnes.name: Congenital sensorineural deafness in English setters in the United Kingdom: prevalence and association with phenotype and sex
pubmed-english-setter-congenital-deafnes.note: Peer-reviewed study (Vet Rec 2020;186(17):e13, Epub 2019-10-29) of 447 UK English Setter puppies from complete litters undergoing BAER testing (2000–2018), reporting 3.6% unilateral and 0.9% bilateral congenital sensorineural deafness (4.5% total).

akc-english-setter-history.name: American Kennel Club — English Setter History: From Net Hunter to Dual-Purpose Show Dog
akc-english-setter-history.note: Historical overview covering 14th-century net-hunting origins, John Caius's 1570 account, Edward Laverack's 1825 line ('Ponto' and 'Old Moll'), R. Purcell Llewellin's field setter line, and 1878 charter recognition.

fci-pyrenean-mastiff-nomenclature.name: FCI Breeds Nomenclature — Mastín del Pirineo (92)
fci-pyrenean-mastiff-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry for Standard No. 92 (Group 2, Section 2.2 Molossoid breeds, Mountain type); documents definitive FCI acceptance on 13 November 1954 and official standard publication on 26 May 1982.

uk-kennel-club-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.name: The Royal Kennel Club — Pyrenean Mastiff (Imp) Breed Information & Interim Standard
uk-kennel-club-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.note: Official UK Kennel Club breed profile and interim standard overview (Working Group, Imported Breed Register since 2001); documents historical name 'Navarra Mastiff', Aragon/Navarre origin, spiked collar history, ideal heights of 81 cm (32 in) for males and 73.5 cm (29 in) for females, and exercise/living space requirements.

akc-pyrenean-mastiff-profile.name: American Kennel Club — Pyrenean Mastiff
akc-pyrenean-mastiff-profile.note: Official AKC breed profile; reports height (30–31 in males, 28–30 in females), weight (120–190 lbs / 54.4–86.2 kg), life expectancy (10–12 years), very low prey drive, puppy diet duration (18 months for females, 24 months for males), and recommended health tests.

pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.name: Pyrenean Mastiff Association of America — Breed Standard & History
pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-standard.note: AKC parent club breed history and standard; documents 1970s breed rescue in Aragon by Rafael Malo Alcrudo (30 foundation dogs from ~100 survivors, 1977 CMPE founding), 1996 US introduction, minimum heights of 30 in (dogs) and 28 in (bitches) with no upper limit, 9:10 proportion, and accepted patch colours including brindle, agouti, sable, and badger.

pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-health.name: Pyrenean Mastiff Association of America — Health Conditions
pmaa-pyrenean-mastiff-health.note: Detailed parent-club health epidemiology covering international hip and elbow dysplasia screening data (Finland n=291, Spain n=82, US/Canada n=81), Finnish Kennel Club cardiac mortality records (1990–2025: 46 cardiac deaths = 6.25%, mean age 6y 10m; last 15 yrs = 6.61%, mean age 5y 10m), degenerative myelopathy, eye conditions (iris-to-iris PPM, entropion, ectropion, distichiasis/trichiasis), and spine conditions (spondylosis, LTV).

petmd-pyrenean-mastiff-health.name: PetMD — Pyrenean Mastiff Dog Breed Health and Care
petmd-pyrenean-mastiff-health.note: Veterinary breed guide reviewed by Barri J. Morrison, DVM (featuring interviews with PMAA president Karina Whittington and board member Crystal Kaiser); verifies 120–190 lb adult weight, 8–12 year lifespan, DM, hip/elbow dysplasia, osteosarcoma, bloat/GDV precautions, feeding frequency (3 meals/day for puppies until ~2 years, 2 meals/day for adults), and grooming schedule.

akc-tibetan-terrier-standard.name: American Kennel Club — Official Standard of the Tibetan Terrier
akc-tibetan-terrier-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard approved 10 March 1987; specifies square proportions, large flat round snowshoe feet, fall of hair over eyes, double coat, any colour/combination with black nose and dark eye rims, average male height 15–16 inches (14–17 inches acceptable, females slightly smaller), and weight 18–30 pounds (14–30 pounds across 14–16 inch heights).

ttca-tibetan-terrier-health-testing.name: Tibetan Terrier Club of America — Health Testing Recommendations
ttca-tibetan-terrier-health-testing.note: Parent-club breeding health recommendations covering hip evaluation, ACVO eye examination, DNA testing for NCL (ATP13A2), PLL (ADAMTS17), PRA3 (FAM161A), and RCD4 PRA (C2orf71), BAER hearing evaluation, and patellar luxation assessment. Note: TTCA has migrated active web operations to https://ttca-online.org/.

fci-bullmastiff-nomenclature.name: FCI - Bullmastiff Breed Nomenclature No. 157
fci-bullmastiff-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry No. 157 confirming Great Britain origin, Group 2 Section 2.1 (Molossian type, Mastiff type) classification without working trial, definitive acceptance on 1955-04-23, official valid standard date 2026-09-08, and English standard publication on 2026-10-06.

american-bullmastiff-association-about-t.name: American Bullmastiff Association - About the Breed & AKC Breed Standard
american-bullmastiff-association-about-t.note: Official parent-club breed overview and AKC standard (approved 8 February 1992, effective 31 March 1992) detailing the 60% Mastiff / 40% Bulldog foundation, 1860 English estate history, 1924 UK and October 1933/1934 US recognition, 8–10 year lifespan, height (males 25–27 in, females 24–26 in), weight (males 110–130 lbs, females 100–120 lbs), and opposite-sex multi-dog household advice.

american-bullmastiff-association-getting.name: American Bullmastiff Association - Getting to Know the Bullmastiff
american-bullmastiff-association-getting.note: Parent-club temperament and FAQ guide covering guardian disposition, drooling, size variations (85 lb females to 170+ lb males outside standard ranges), adult feeding volume (2–3 cups of dry kibble twice daily, or 40–60 lbs/month), obedience training, and avoiding high-impact activities until well over 18 months of age.

akc-bullmastiff-history.name: American Kennel Club - Bullmastiff History: From World-Class Protector to Family Companion
akc-bullmastiff-history.note: Historical feature by Denise Flaim detailing 'The Gamekeeper's Night Dog', William Burton's Thorneywood Kennels and Thorneywood Terror's undefeated one-pound wager, nighttime patrol communication via forehead wrinkling, and the Rockefeller family's 1934 import of Bullmastiffs to their Pocantico estate.

northern-bullmastiff-club-about-the-bree.name: The Northern Bullmastiff Club - About the Bullmastiff
northern-bullmastiff-club-about-the-bree.note: UK breed-club history and care guide documenting historical names ('Bull and Mastiff dog', 'Gamekeeper's Night Dog', 'Bull-Mastiff'), the 1900 Gamekeepers' Dog Show, S. E. Moseley's Farcroft Kennels and 'Moseley Recipe', 1924 UK recognition and 1928 first champions (Ch. Farcroft Silvo and Ch. Tiger Prince), same-sex dog intolerance at maturity, low alone-time tolerance, and slobber/drool.

bullmastiff-lymphoma-gwas-mortlock-2023.name: Genomic Analysis of Lymphoma Risk in Bullmastiff Dogs
bullmastiff-lymphoma-gwas-mortlock-2023.note: Peer-reviewed genome-wide association study (Mortlock et al., Vet Sci 2023;10(12):703, PMID: 38133254, PMCID: PMC10747964) of Bullmastiff lymphoma (average diagnosis age <6 years in 55 cases; 49 genotyped cases vs. 281 controls), identifying risk-associated regions on chromosomes 13 (MYC / PVT1) and 33 (SENP7 / NFKBIZ).

american-kennel-club-gordon-setter.name: American Kennel Club - Gordon Setter
american-kennel-club-gordon-setter.note: Breed profile covering size, life expectancy, temperament, exercise, grooming, history, nutrition, and health.

fci-gordon-setter-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 6 - Gordon Setter
fci-gordon-setter-standard.note: Current English FCI standard published 6 October 2026; includes origin, classification, temperament, coat, colour, height, and weight.

gordon-setter-club-of-america-health-sta.name: Gordon Setter Club of America - Health Statement

ach-romanian-bucovina-shepherd-standard-.name: Asociația Chinologică Română - Standard Ciobănesc Românesc de Bucovina
ach-romanian-bucovina-shepherd-standard-.note: Official Romanian Kennel Club (AChR) breed standard documenting the traditional names 'Dulău' and 'Căpău', the first 1982 AChR standard, the 2001 and 29 March 2002 updates, and the 22 August 2004 Gura Humorului revision with FCI representatives Raymond Triquet and Bernard Denis.

ach-dysplasia-screening-list.name: Asociația Chinologică Română - Anexa 3: Lista Raselor Supuse Testelor de Displazie (HD, ED, SP)
ach-dysplasia-screening-list.note: Official Romanian Kennel Club (AChR) breeding regulation table (adopted 17 February 2016) listing Ciobănesc Românesc de Bucovina (No. 357, Group II) for radiographic hip dysplasia (HD, minimum age 12 months, accepted breeding grade up to C) and elbow dysplasia (ED, minimum age 12 months, accepted breeding grade up to 1) evaluation.

ach-dysplasia-info.name: Asociația Chinologică Română - Informații Examen Displazie
ach-dysplasia-info.note: Official Romanian Kennel Club (AChR) hip and elbow dysplasia evaluation protocol detailing GRSK-accredited radiographic scoring recognized by the FCI Scientific Commission and International Elbow Working Group (IEWG).

ach-selection-regulation-romanian-shephe.name: Asociația Chinologică Română - Regulament de Selecție pentru Ciobăneștii Românești
ach-selection-regulation-romanian-shephe.note: Official AChR breeding-selection regulation (adopted 20 August 2008, effective 21 August 2008) requiring all Romanian Shepherd breeding stock (minimum age 15 months, microchipped) to pass a two-judge selection examination (ADR) covering body measurements, coat/undercoat, pigmentation, complete dentition/bite, calm balanced character, gait, and any requested medical/radiographic certificates prior to Romanian Stud Book (COR) litter registration.

ach-romanian-shepherd-breeds-2025-commun.name: Asociația Chinologică Română - Comunicat Oficial privind Rasele de Ciobănești Românești (2025)
ach-romanian-shepherd-breeds-2025-commun.note: Official AChR press release (No. 881/29.10.2025) reporting Romanian Stud Book (COR) registration totals for 2020–2024 (5,668 Romanian shepherd dogs total, led by 1,984 Ciobănesc Românesc de Bucovina registrations) and confirming 2009 provisional and 2019 definitive FCI recognition.

romfilatelia-romanian-dog-breeds-2019.publisher: Romfilatelia (Romanian Post Philatelic Authority, with AChR and Grigore Antipa National Museum)
romfilatelia-romanian-dog-breeds-2019.note: Official 22 February 2019 Romanian postage stamp issue (prepared with the Romanian Kennel Club and Grigore Antipa National Museum of Natural History) featuring the Romanian Bucovina Shepherd Dog on the Lei 8.50 stamp.

wisdom-panel-romanian-bucovina-shepherd-.name: Wisdom Panel - Romanian Bucovina Shepherd Dog
wisdom-panel-romanian-bucovina-shepherd-.note: Veterinary-reviewed breed profile (reviewed 12 July 2023 by Dr. Casey Knox, DVM) documenting traditional names ('Dulău' and 'Căpău'), transhumance flock guarding against wolves, bears, and lynx, the traditional wooden 'jujău' neck dangle required on free-ranging working dogs in Romania, 1982 AChR standard and 2019 recognition, and secondary weight (110–198 lb) and lifespan (12–14 yr) estimates.

boykin-spaniel-society-breed-standard.note: Official breed standard of The Boykin Spaniel Society (founded 1977; studbook established 1979), specifying height (15.5–18 in dogs, 14–16.5 in bitches), weight (30–40 lbs dogs, 25–35 lbs bitches), coat varieties (including short straight coat without feathering for warm-weather hunting), and working retriever/flusher characteristics.

boykin-spaniel-society-preferred-breeder.name: The Boykin Spaniel Society - Preferred Breeder Program Booklet (Revision 5)
boykin-spaniel-society-preferred-breeder.note: Official Boykin Spaniel Society Preferred Breeder Program requirements (Revision 5, June 2023), mandating OFA Fair-or-better hip evaluations, Normal cardiac, patellar, and ophthalmic certifications, and DNA testing for EIC, DM, and CEA with at least one parent tested Clear per condition.

boykin-spaniel-society-faq.name: The Boykin Spaniel Society - Frequently Asked Questions & Health Overview
boykin-spaniel-society-faq.note: Official Boykin Spaniel Society FAQ covering companion and hunting suitability, skin allergies in certain bloodlines, hip dysplasia, juvenile cataracts, pulmonic stenosis (congenital cardiac screening), patellar luxation, EIC, CEA, and DM inheritance tables.

boykin-spaniel-club-faq.name: Boykin Spaniel Club and Breeders Association of America - Breed FAQs
boykin-spaniel-club-faq.publisher: Boykin Spaniel Club and Breeders Association of America
boykin-spaniel-club-faq.note: AKC parent club FAQ detailing upland and waterfowl hunting versatility, high daily energy, sociability with children and other dogs, and moderate alert barking.

uc-davis-vgl-boykin-spaniel-health-panel.name: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory - Boykin Spaniel Health Panel
uc-davis-vgl-boykin-spaniel-health-panel.note: Veterinary genetics laboratory breed health panel for the Boykin Spaniel covering Chondrodystrophy (CDDY/IVDD — FGF4-12) and Chondrodysplasia (CDPA — FGF4-18), Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA — NHEJ1), Degenerative Myelopathy (DM — SOD1), Exercise-Induced Collapse (EIC — DNM1), and Progressive Rod-Cone Degeneration (PRA-prcd — PRCD).

boykin-spaniel-eic-dnm1-study-2011.name: Minor et al. (2011) - Presence and Impact of the Exercise-Induced Collapse Associated DNM1 Mutation in Labrador Retrievers and Other Breeds
boykin-spaniel-eic-dnm1-study-2011.note: Peer-reviewed genetic survey (Vet J 2011;189(2):214–219, PMID: 21782486, DOI: 10.1016/j.tvjl.2011.06.022) confirming the DNM1 c.767G>T mutation and clinical exercise-induced collapse phenotype in Boykin Spaniels.

canine-fgf4-ivdd-batcher-2019.name: Batcher et al. (2019) - Phenotypic Effects of FGF4 Retrogenes on Intervertebral Disc Disease in Dogs
canine-fgf4-ivdd-batcher-2019.note: Peer-reviewed study (Genes 2019;10(6):435, PMCID: PMC6627552, DOI: 10.3390/genes10060435) demonstrating that the chromosome 12 FGF4 retrogene insertion (12-FGF4RG / CDDY) acts dominantly to cause premature intervertebral disc calcification and elevated risk of Hansen Type I disc herniation in segregating breeds including the Boykin Spaniel.

petmd-boykin-spaniel-health-care.name: PetMD - Boykin Spaniel Dog Breed Health and Care
petmd-boykin-spaniel-health-care.note: Veterinary breed care guide covering Boykin Spaniel exercise needs (at least 60 minutes daily), weekly brushing, monthly bathing limit, summer coat trimming for swimmers, post-swim ear flushing, and inherited health screening.

societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-pr.name: Société Centrale Canine — Chien d'Artois Breed Profile
societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-pr.note: Official French national kennel-club breed profile covering general appearance, height (53–58 cm), weight (28–30 kg), coat, history, pack behaviour (entering the pack from 6 months of age, firm yet gentle 'iron hand in a velvet glove' guidance), unsuitability for urban living or being tied up, and puppy/adult nutrition (growing until 1 year of age on two substantial meals per day).

societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-hi.name: Société Centrale Canine — Le chien d'Artois : l'histoire
societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-hi.note: In-depth historical dossier (published 5 December 2022, updated 4 November 2025) documenting 1394 and 1410 Burgundian Ducal account mentions, the 1431 Paris coronation stag hunt before Henry VI, Louis XIII's 1608–1610 journals, 1609 Croÿ gift, Sélincourt (1683), Le Couteulx de Canteleu (1890), Ernest Levoir's Rallye-Scardon (c. 1888–1918), Auguste and Albert Mallart (1854–1932), the 1930 suppression of 'Briquet', and the 1970s reconstruction by André Audréchy ('du Parc à Biches'), Joseph Mancini, and Josette Pilat ('La Meute Saint-Louis' / 'Piqu'Artois Saint-Louis').

societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-ch.name: Société Centrale Canine — Le chien d'Artois : le caractère et la fonctionnalité
societe-centrale-canine-chien-dartois-ch.note: Official SCC working and temperament dossier (published 5 December 2022, updated 4 November 2025) detailing cold-trail 'rapprocheur' ability (up to 6-hour-old trails), vocalization ('meowing' whimpers on cold scent before giving full voice), puppy initiation at 4–5 months, pack peacefulness (including same-sex dogs), affectionate and quiet demeanour off-duty, TAN/brevet de chasse working trials, and current usage (~75% on wild boar, plus hare and roe deer).

royal-canin-fr-chien-dartois.name: Royal Canin France — Chien d'Artois
royal-canin-fr-chien-dartois.note: French breed guide listing average life expectancy (10–13 years), temperament traits (affectionate, confident, gentle, calm, intelligent, loyal), moderate grooming needs, high exercise needs, and early training.

woopets-chien-dartois.name: Woopets — Chien d'Artois : caractère, santé, alimentation, prix et entretien

fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-nomenclature.name: FCI - Gammel Dansk Hønsehund (Old Danish Pointing Dog) Nomenclature No. 281
fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-nomenclature.note: Official FCI nomenclature entry No. 281 confirming Denmark origin, Group 7 Section 1.1 (Continental Pointing Dogs, 'Braque' type) subject to a working trial, definitive acceptance on 1969-04-02, valid standard date 1998-01-08, and official multilingual names (Gammel Dansk Hønsehund, Old Danish Pointing Dog, Chien d'arrêt danois ancestral, Altdänischer Vorstehhund, Antiguo Perro de Muestra Danés).

fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-judges-compe.name: FCI & Klubben for Gamle Danske Hønsehunde — Judges' Compendium for the Old Danish Pointer (FCI Standard No. 281)
fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-judges-compe.publisher: Fédération Cynologique Internationale / Klubben for Gamle Danske Hønsehunde
fci-old-danish-pointing-dog-judges-compe.note: Official FCI breed-specific education compendium (March 2026) providing detailed illustrated commentary on FCI Standard No. 281, including complete 42-tooth dentition (20 upper, 22 lower), puppy-to-adult eye colour darkening, ear length (leaving just over the outer third of the muzzle free), throat dewlap hallmark, 50%/50% chest depth, 110°/125°/135° angulation, and faults/disqualifications.

danish-kennel-club-old-danish-pointing-d.name: Dansk Kennel Klub (DKK) — Gammel Dansk Hønsehund Breed Profile & Breeding Requirements
danish-kennel-club-old-danish-pointing-d.note: Official Danish Kennel Club breed profile and mandatory pre-breeding studbook regulations ('Avlskrav': mandatory pre-mating HD status A or B, or HD C only if mated to HD A; mandatory pre-mating rcd4/PRA DNA test status; documented normal testicles; and Basis+ GDH breeding permit introduced 1 September 2017).

danish-breed-club-breeding-approval.name: Klubben for Gamle Danske Hønsehunde — Hvad skal der til for at få sin hund avlsgodkendt?
danish-breed-club-breeding-approval.note: Official Danish breed-club 5-point breeding approval checklist: (1) minimum 'Good' show rating at ≥15 months of age, (2) official DKK hip dysplasia grading A, B, or C, (3) DNA status for congenital myasthenic syndrome ('muskeltræthed'), (4) hunting evaluation ('jagtlig vurdering') for both sexes, and (5) DNA test status for PRA.

old-danish-pointing-dog-pra-c17h2orf71-s.name: Karlskov-Mortensen et al. (2018) — Identification of the mutation causing progressive retinal atrophy in Old Danish Pointing Dog
old-danish-pointing-dog-pra-c17h2orf71-s.note: Peer-reviewed genomic study (Anim Genet. 2018 Jun;49(3):237-241, PMID 29624701) identifying the autosomal recessive single-base insertion c.3149_3150insC in exon 1 of C17H2orf71 (C2orf71 / PCARE, rcd4-PRA) as the cause of late-onset progressive retinal atrophy diagnosed in the Old Danish Pointing Dog since the late 1990s.

old-danish-pointing-dog-cms-chat-study.name: Proschowsky et al. (2007) — Identification of a mutation in the CHAT gene of Old Danish Pointing Dogs affected with congenital myasthenic syndrome
old-danish-pointing-dog-cms-chat-study.note: Peer-reviewed study (J Hered. 2007;98(5):539-543, PMID 17586598) identifying an autosomal recessive G-to-A missense mutation (valine-to-methionine substitution) in exon 6 of the choline acetyltransferase (CHAT) gene causing congenital myasthenic syndrome ('muskeltræthed') in Old Danish Pointing Dogs and establishing a breed-specific DNA test.

old-danish-pointing-dog-cms-clinical-stu.name: Flagstad et al. (1989) — Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome in the Dog Breed Gammel Dansk Hønsehund
old-danish-pointing-dog-cms-clinical-stu.note: Peer-reviewed clinical, electrophysiological, pharmacological, and immunological study (Acta Vet Scand. 1989;30(1):89-102, PMID 2782236 / PMCID PMC8142211) demonstrating a presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome without acetylcholine-receptor antibodies in the Gammel Dansk Hønsehund.

danish-dog-breeds-genetic-profile-study.name: Pertoldi et al. (2013) — Characterization of the genetic profile of five Danish dog breeds
danish-dog-breeds-genetic-profile-study.note: Peer-reviewed population genetics study (J Anim Sci. 2013 Nov;91(11):5122-5127, PMID 23989866) quantifying within-breed expected heterozygosity and genetic differentiation across five native Danish dog breeds including the Old Danish Pointing Dog.

wikimedia-old-danish-pointer-pleple2000.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Wyżeł duński 123.jpg
wikimedia-old-danish-pointer-pleple2000.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Wyżeł duński 123.jpg' (2118 × 2082 px), photographed by Pleple2000 on 2006-11-12 at the World Dog Show in Poznań and published under CC BY-SA 3.0 / CC BY-SA 2.5 / GFDL 1.2+.

wikimedia-old-danish-pointer-canarian.name: Wikimedia Commons — File:Old Danish Pointer.jpg
wikimedia-old-danish-pointer-canarian.note: Wikimedia Commons file page for 'File:Old Danish Pointer.jpg' (496 × 319 px), photographed by Canarian on 2008-10-31 and uploaded on 2013-10-23 under CC BY-SA 3.0.

fci-aidi-official-standard.name: FCI — Atlas Mountain Dog (Aidi), Standard No. 247
fci-aidi-official-standard.note: The standard PDF is dated 05.05.2003. The FCI nomenclature page separately lists 25.03.2003 as the publication date of the official valid standard.

united-kennel-club-aidi-standard.name: United Kennel Club — Aidi (Atlas Mountain Dog) Official Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-aidi-standard.note: The PDF identifies itself as the official UKC breed standard, revised January 1, 2008.

royal-canin-aidi-profile.name: Royal Canin India — Aidi Breed Profile
royal-canin-aidi-profile.note: Used for the published average life-expectancy estimate; not treated as an official breed standard.

pubmed-aidi-leishmaniasis-study.name: Diagnosis and Prevalence of Canine Leishmaniasis in the Atlas Shepherd Dog
pubmed-aidi-leishmaniasis-study.publisher: PubMed / Veterinary Parasitology: Regional Studies and Reports
pubmed-aidi-leishmaniasis-study.note: Study of 161 Atlas shepherd dogs in the Tiaret region of Algeria; findings are specific to the study population and location.

fci-puli-official-standard.name: FCI — Puli, Standard No. 55
fci-puli-official-standard.note: Official valid standard; FCI nomenclature lists 29 October 2013 as its publication date.

american-kennel-club-puli.note: Breed overview, coat care and recommended health tests.

puli-club-of-america-health-statement.note: Breed-club health-screening recommendations for breeding stock.

puli-club-of-america-faq.name: Puli Club of America — Frequently Asked Questions
puli-club-of-america-faq.note: Used for the club's published average lifespan estimate and health-screening information.

enci-cane-da-pastore-abruzzese-maremmano.name: ENCI - Cane da Pastore Abruzzese Maremmano (FCI 201)
enci-cane-da-pastore-abruzzese-maremmano.note: Italian national kennel club breed monograph and Riproduzione Selezionata requirements: minimum age 18 months, minimum conformation qualification Molto Buono at a breed specialty or gathering, CPMA morphological-character test (TEST T.M.C. CPMA), hip dysplasia grade HD A or B, and elbow dysplasia grade ED 0 or 1; also documents Roman and medieval historical sources, the 1952 Brescia specialty, the 1958-01-01 unified standard, foundational kennels, and puppy weaning/development.

ukc-maremma-sheepdog-standard.name: United Kennel Club - Maremma Sheepdog Official Breed Standard
ukc-maremma-sheepdog-standard.note: UKC breed standard (recognized 2006-07-01, revised 2017-05-01) placing the breed in the Guardian Dog Group and recording the traditional pre-2025 size ranges (males 25.5–28.75 in / 77–100 lb; females 23.5–26.5 in / 66–88 lb) and tolerance of cropped ears only in working herd-guarding dogs.

rkc-maremma-sheepdog-breed-information.name: The Royal Kennel Club - Maremma Sheepdog Breed Information & Health Standard
rkc-maremma-sheepdog-breed-information.note: UK kennel club breed guide placing the Maremma Sheepdog in the Pastoral Group (Breed Watch Category 2), listing large size, over 2 hours of daily exercise, lifespan over 10 years, and Best Practice pre-breeding hip screening under the BVA/KC Hip Dysplasia Scheme.

warrnambool-middle-island-maremma-projec.name: Warrnambool Penguins - Maremma Dogs and the Middle Island Project
warrnambool-middle-island-maremma-projec.note: Official Warrnambool City Council conservation project documentation confirming that Maremma guardian dogs (beginning in 2006 with Eudy and Tula, named after Eudyptula minor) have protected Middle Island's Little Penguin colony from red foxes.

talenti-2023-italian-lgd-herding-selecti.name: Selection Signatures in Italian Livestock Guardian and Herding Shepherd Dogs (Veterinary Sciences, 2023)
talenti-2023-italian-lgd-herding-selecti.note: Open-access genomic study (170K canine SNP array across 158 dogs from 4 Italian livestock guardian and 5 herding shepherd breeds, including 20 Maremma and Abruzzi Sheepdogs) identifying selection signatures differentiating flock guardians from herding dogs around genes linked to body size/muscle development (MAP2K5, RYR3), drop vs. prick ear morphology (WIF1, MSRB3), behaviour (LLPH), and eye development.

donner-2023-canine-mendelian-disease-var.name: Genetic prevalence and clinical relevance of canine Mendelian disease variants in over one million dogs (PLOS Genetics, 2023)
donner-2023-canine-mendelian-disease-var.note: Open-access study (Donner et al., 2023, Table 2) reporting the Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA, OMIA Variant ID 632 / NHEJ1 intronic deletion) disease-associated allele at a 2.7% variant frequency in screened Maremma Sheepdogs (N = 37 dogs).

rombola-2021-leishmania-lazio-dogs.name: Seroprevalence and risk factors associated with exposure to Leishmania infantum in dogs, in an endemic Mediterranean region (PLOS ONE, 2021)
rombola-2021-leishmania-lazio-dogs.note: Open-access epidemiological study of 13,292 canine sera collected in Lazio, central Italy (2010–2014), finding that autochthonous Maremma Sheepdogs and long-coated dogs had significantly lower odds of Leishmania infantum seropositivity compared with non-autochthonous breeds (OR = 1.9 for other breeds vs. Maremma Sheepdog, p < 0.001).

fci-portuguese-water-dog-standard.name: FCI — Standard No. 37: Portuguese Water Dog
fci-portuguese-water-dog-standard.note: Official valid standard publication date is 4 November 2008; the English PDF bears the date 30 March 2009.

portuguese-kennel-club-portuguese-water-.name: Clube Português de Canicultura — Portuguese Water Dog
portuguese-kennel-club-portuguese-water-.note: Portuguese breed profile with FCI classification, measurements and historical summary.

american-kennel-club-portuguese-water-do.name: American Kennel Club — Portuguese Water Dog
american-kennel-club-portuguese-water-do.note: Breed overview, coat and grooming information, and national breed-club health-testing recommendations.

portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-hea.name: Portuguese Water Dog Club of America — Health Overview
portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-hea.publisher: Portuguese Water Dog Club of America
portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-hea.note: Breed-club overview of reported health issues and recommended pre-breeding evaluations and genetic tests.

portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-car.name: Portuguese Water Dog Club of America — Breed and Owner Guidance
portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-car.publisher: Portuguese Water Dog Club of America
portuguese-water-dog-club-of-america-car.note: Owner guidance on activity, training, family life, grooming, shedding and allergy considerations.

american-kennel-club-hovawart.name: American Kennel Club — Hovawart Breed Information
american-kennel-club-hovawart.note: AKC Foundation Stock Service breed profile (recorded in FSS since October 2010, assigned to the Working Group) listing height (23–28 in), weight (65–90 lbs), lifespan (10–14 years), low drooling level, exercise needs (at least a 1-hour walk plus 3–4 shorter daily walks), and hip dysplasia rates under 5%.

hovawart-club-of-great-britain-origins.name: Hovawart Club of Great Britain — Origins of the Hovawart (Dr. Jens Kerl Studbook Research)
hovawart-club-of-great-britain-origins.note: Summary of archival studbook research by Dr. Jens Kerl presented at the International Hovawart Federation (IHF) centenary, showing that Kurt König founded the Hovawart-Verein für Deutsche Schutzhunde in Thale in January 1924, that all modern lines trace to the 1932 sire Castor Meyer-Busch, and that modern bloodlines comprise ~65% regional farm 'Typenhunde', 20.2% German Shepherd Dog, and 14.8% Newfoundland (with Kuvasz used only in pre-WWI trials lost in the war).

mandrioli-2021-hovawart-degenerative-mye.name: Degenerative Myelopathy in Hovawart Dogs: Molecular Characterization, Pathological Features and Accumulation of Mutant Superoxide Dismutase 1 Protein (Journal of Comparative Pathology, 2021)
mandrioli-2021-hovawart-degenerative-mye.note: Mandrioli et al. (2021, doi:10.1016/j.jcpa.2020.11.006) molecular and neuropathological study of Hovawart dogs aged 9–12 years with progressive pelvic-limb ataxia and paraparesis, confirming homozygosity for SOD1:c.118G>A (p.E40K) and mutant SOD1 accumulation in spinal cord neurons and astrocytes without the SP110 risk haplotype.

ahlgren-uimari-2016-hovawart-hypothyroid.name: Heritability of hypothyroidism in the Finnish Hovawart population (Acta Veterinaria Scandinavica, 2016)
ahlgren-uimari-2016-hovawart-hypothyroid.publisher: Acta Veterinaria Scandinavica / PubMed Central (PMCID: PMC4897810; PMID: 27267591)
ahlgren-uimari-2016-hovawart-hypothyroid.note: Open-access genetic study (Åhlgren & Uimari, 2016, CC BY 4.0) of 4,953 Finnish Hovawarts born 1990–2010 estimating moderate-to-high heritability for hypothyroidism (h² = 0.47 via REML to 0.62 via Bayesian Gibbs sampling) and noting a 13% prevalence of autoimmune lymphocytic thyroiditis markers in Swedish Hovawarts (Ferm et al., 2009).

wikimedia-hovawart-three-colours-oxborro.note: Photograph showing all three permitted coat colours of the Hovawart (black and gold, blond, and black) by Oxborrow, captured 2009-03-03 (Canon EOS 400D) and uploaded 2009-06-13, 3,888 × 2,592 pixels, released into the public domain worldwide.

wikimedia-hovawart-black-and-tan-faigl.note: Photograph of a black-and-gold (schwarzmarken) Hovawart by Ladislav Faigl (Faigl.ladislav), uploaded 2006-04-30, 640 × 480 pixels, licensed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported (and dual-licensed under GFDL 1.2+).

fci-chinese-crested-dog-standard.name: FCI — Chinese Crested Dog Official Breed Standard No. 288
fci-chinese-crested-dog-standard.note: Official English FCI Standard No. 288. The PDF is dated 15 September 2021 and states 27 July 2021 as the publication date of the official valid standard. Used for origin, classification, utilization, varieties, coat, temperament, dentition, and ideal height.

american-kennel-club-chinese-crested-dog.name: American Kennel Club — Chinese Crested Dog
american-kennel-club-chinese-crested-dog.note: Breed profile consulted for life expectancy, grooming differences, skin care, and recommended breed health tests.

american-kennel-club-chinese-crested-his.name: American Kennel Club — Chinese Crested History
american-kennel-club-chinese-crested-his.note: Historical overview covering uncertainty around early origins, historical names, the work of Ida Garrett and Debra Woods, formation of the American Chinese Crested Club, and AKC recognition.

american-chinese-crested-club-health-sta.name: American Chinese Crested Club — Health Statement
american-chinese-crested-club-health-sta.note: Breed-club health statement approved on 1 October 2018. Lists recommended eye, cardiac, patella, prcd-PRA, primary lens luxation, and PRA-rcd3 screening.

ecvo-chinese-crested-hereditary-eye-dise.name: ECVO Manual — Chinese Crested Dog: Known and Presumed Hereditary Eye Diseases
ecvo-chinese-crested-hereditary-eye-dise.note: The 2021 ECVO manual entry lists known or presumed inherited ocular disorders and distinguishes conditions with identified inheritance or genetic tests from those whose inheritance is unknown.

Used for classification, origin, historical summary, hunting purpose, temperament, coat, colour, and height.

vdh-griffon-bleu-de-gascogne.note: German kennel-club breed profile consulted to cross-check FCI classification, height, appearance, coat pattern, temperament, and historical origin.

united-kennel-club-griffon-bleu-de-gasco.name: United Kennel Club — Griffon Bleu de Gascogne Breed Standard
united-kennel-club-griffon-bleu-de-gasco.note: Breed standard consulted for a secondary comparison of coat, colour, head and body features, temperament, and height. Registry-specific wording and measurements should not be treated as interchangeable with every other standard.

zoetis-braque-saint-germain.note: Veterinary-company breed profile reporting an estimated life-span range of 10–14 years and summarising broad health-topic categories. The categories are not treated as proof of breed-specific disease prevalence.

royal-canin-braque-saint-germain.name: Royal Canin — Braque Saint-Germain Breed Profile
royal-canin-braque-saint-germain.note: Breed profile covering historical development, hunting role, temperament, and an estimated life expectancy of 12–13 years. Lifespan figures are presented as estimates rather than guaranteed outcomes.

akc-english-setter-standard.name: American Kennel Club — Official Standard for the English Setter
akc-english-setter-standard.note: Official AKC breed standard approved November 11, 1986; specifies dogs about 25 inches, bitches about 24 inches, and belton coat colors.

fci-english-setter-standard.name: FCI-Standard N° 2 — English Setter
fci-english-setter-standard.note: Official FCI Standard No. 2 (Group 7, Section 2.2); specifies height of 65–68 cm for males and 61–65 cm for females, plus belton coat colors and working trial requirement.

esaa-health-genetics.name: English Setter Association of America — Health & Genetics (CHIC & BAER)

esaa-breed-faqs.name: English Setter Association of America — Frequently Asked Questions About English Setters
esaa-breed-faqs.note: Parent club FAQ covering temperament, grooming, field vs. bench lines, hypothyroidism, allergies, and congenital deafness.

pubmed-english-setter-cln8-ncl.name: A mutation in the CLN8 gene in English Setter dogs with neuronal ceroid-lipofuscinosis
pubmed-english-setter-cln8-ncl.publisher: Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications / PubMed
pubmed-english-setter-cln8-ncl.note: Peer-reviewed study identifying the autosomal recessive CLN8 c.491T>C (p.L164P) missense mutation responsible for hereditary neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (NCL8) in English Setters.

ofa-rcd4-pra.name: Orthopedic Foundation for Animals — RCD4 Progressive Retinal Atrophy
ofa-rcd4-pra.note: OFA and Animal Health Trust overview of late-onset rod-cone dysplasia 4 (rcd4-PRA, C2orf71 mutation), an autosomal recessive retinal degeneration averaging ~10 years at diagnosis in English Setters and other breeds.

fci-schipperke-standard.name: FCI Standard No. 83 - Schipperke
fci-schipperke-standard.note: FCI Standard No. 83. The PDF is dated 20 January 2010 and identifies 28 July 2009 as the publication date of the official valid standard.

overview.summary: The Afghan Hound is a tall, athletic sighthound recognised for its long, silky coat, distinctive topknot, narrow head and dignified expression. Bred for hunting in challenging terrain, it combines speed and keen sight with an independent, often reserved personality.
overview.description: Elegant in appearance but built for athletic movement, the Afghan Hound has a long, fine-textured coat, a flowing topknot and prominent hipbones. Its coat can appear in many colours, and the shorter-haired saddle on mature dogs is a characteristic feature of the breed. Afghan Hounds are often affectionate with familiar people while remaining independent or aloof with strangers. Their hunting heritage means they may pursue animals that move quickly, so reliable management, secure fencing and careful off-lead decisions are important. The coat takes substantial ongoing care: regular, thorough brushing and bathing help prevent tangles and mats. Prospective owners should be prepared for both the grooming commitment and the need for safe opportunities to move and run.
overview.history: The Afghan Hound is an ancient type of sighthound associated with Afghanistan, where dogs of this form were used to hunt game in varied and often rugged landscapes. Its speed, sight and agility suited it to pursuing quarry across open ground. The modern pedigree breed was developed further in Britain after Afghan-type hounds were brought to the country, and it later became established in conformation showing and as a companion. The precise early ancestry is not fully documented, so specific origin stories should be treated cautiously.
overview.originalPurpose: A sighthound used to pursue and catch game by sight and speed in open or rugged terrain.
currentRoles: Lure coursing and other suitable sighthound sports
Reward-based training and scent or enrichment games

physical.sizeCategory: Large, tall and lightly built sighthound
physical.coatType: Long, fine, silky hair over much of the body, with a long topknot and feathering. Mature dogs characteristically have shorter, close-lying hair over the saddle of the back.
physical.coatLength: Long, silky and feathered, with a short-haired saddle
coatColors: Other solid colours and combinations permitted by the applicable breed standard
physical.sheddingLevel: Loose hair can be less conspicuous than on many short-coated breeds, but the long coat can tangle and mat. Regular brushing and bathing are needed to maintain coat condition.
distinctiveFeatures: Long, silky topknot on the head
Long, hanging ears covered with silky hair
Narrow, refined head and dark, almond-shaped eyes
Long coat with prominent feathering
Short, close-lying saddle on the back of mature dogs
Tall, athletic frame with prominent hipbones and long limbs
High-carried tail that typically has a ring or curl at the end

traits: Independent
Dignified
Often reserved with unfamiliar people
Affectionate with familiar people
Sensitive to rough handling
Athletic and fast-moving
Can be strongly attracted to moving animals
May be less consistently responsive when distracted

exercise.level: High
activities: Daily walks with opportunities to explore safely
Supervised running in a securely enclosed area
Age-appropriate lure coursing or other sighthound activities
Short reward-based training sessions
Food puzzles and other calm mental enrichment

grooming.brushing: Brush and comb the coat thoroughly several times a week, often more frequently depending on its length, texture and condition. Work in small sections and check behind the ears, under the legs, around the chest, between the feathering and along the tail for tangles or mats.
grooming.bathing: Regular bathing is generally needed to keep the long coat clean and manageable. Use dog-appropriate shampoo and conditioner, rinse thoroughly and dry the coat carefully. The appropriate interval depends on the dog's coat, lifestyle and skin condition.
notes: Do not brush only the visible top layer; check through the coat to the skin.
Use a suitable comb to identify knots before they tighten into mats.
Check the ears regularly and follow veterinary advice for cleaning.
Trim nails as needed and brush teeth regularly.
Check the coat after outdoor activity for burrs, grass seeds and debris.
Ask an experienced groomer for help if the coat becomes heavily matted.

training.difficulty: Moderate to challenging; independence and hunting motivation can make reliable responses difficult around distractions.
tips: Use patient, reward-based methods and keep sessions short and engaging.
Practise recall from an early age, but do not rely on it alone around wildlife or roads.
Use a secure enclosed space for off-lead running.
Build attention and calm behaviours gradually in low-distraction settings.
Introduce handling, grooming and bathing positively so coat care becomes routine.
Avoid harsh punishment or forceful handling.
Provide appropriate outlets for running and exploration rather than expecting the dog to remain inactive.
training.socialization: Introduce the puppy gradually and positively to people, dogs, everyday sounds, handling and varied environments. Continue reinforcing calm, safe behaviour throughout adulthood, while respecting the dog's individual comfort level.

climates: Temperate climates with shade, water and appropriate shelter
Cool climates with suitable protection and comfortable resting areas
Warm climates with exercise during cooler hours and close attention to overheating

nutrition.dietType: A complete and balanced diet suitable for the dog's life stage, body condition, activity and individual veterinary needs.

feedingFrequency.puppy: Feed a complete puppy diet in age-appropriate meals, following the food manufacturer's guidance and advice from a veterinarian.
feedingFrequency.adult: Many adult dogs do well with two measured meals daily. Adjust portions to maintain a lean body condition and account for changes in exercise.

nutrition.guidelines: Choose a nutritionally complete food appropriate for the dog's life stage. Measure portions, keep fresh water available, monitor body condition and adjust intake as activity changes. Treats should be included in the daily calorie allowance. Seek veterinary guidance for growth, weight changes or specific dietary needs.
considerations: Avoid overfeeding and monitor body condition regularly.
Adjust food quantity for changes in exercise, age and health.
Introduce diet changes gradually unless a veterinarian advises otherwise.
Discuss supplements or restrictive diets with a veterinarian before using them.
Ask a veterinarian about meal timing and exercise precautions if the dog has risk factors for gastric dilatation-volvulus.
nutrition.note: Individual calorie requirements vary. Use feeding instructions as a starting point, then adjust with body-condition monitoring and veterinary advice.

health.overview: Afghan Hounds need routine preventive veterinary care, weight and dental monitoring, and attention to their eyes, joints and overall condition. Breed-club screening recommendations include hip evaluation, an ophthalmologist evaluation and thyroid evaluation. These tests help assess selected risks; they do not guarantee that a dog is free of inherited or later-developing disease.
commonConditions: Gastric dilatation-volvulus (bloat): a life-threatening emergency involving stomach distension and possible twisting. Seek emergency veterinary care immediately if suspected.
Hip dysplasia: a developmental joint condition for which breed-club screening is recommended.
Eye disorders: an ophthalmologist examination is included in breed-club screening recommendations.
Thyroid disorders: thyroid evaluation is included in breed-club screening recommendations.

Chylothorax: a condition involving accumulation of lymphatic fluid in the chest that has been the subject of breed-club research. This mention does not establish that it is common in every Afghan Hound population.
preventiveCare: Schedule routine veterinary examinations and keep vaccinations and parasite prevention appropriate to local risks.
Maintain a lean body condition and adjust food intake as activity changes.
Discuss breed-club screening records with the breeder and veterinarian.
Seek urgent veterinary care for signs of bloat, including a distended abdomen, unproductive retching, restlessness or sudden deterioration.
Monitor mobility, appetite, energy and other changes, and discuss persistent concerns with a veterinarian.
recommendedScreenings: Hip evaluation
Ophthalmologist evaluation
Thyroid evaluation
Review of relevant health records and screening results with a veterinarian before breeding
health.dentalCare: Brush the teeth regularly with dog-specific dental products and arrange veterinary dental assessment when indicated. Do not use human toothpaste.
health.earCare: Check the long, hair-covered ears regularly for odour, redness, discharge or discomfort. Clean only as advised by a veterinarian and seek care if signs of infection appear.
health.skinCare: Part the coat to inspect the skin during grooming. Look for redness, parasites, irritation and mats that pull on the skin. Seek veterinary advice for persistent itching, sores or hair loss.

idealFor: Owners prepared for substantial, ongoing coat care
People who can provide daily exercise and safe opportunities to run
Households that appreciate an independent dog and use patient training
Owners able to manage a strong chase instinct responsibly
People interested in sighthound sports or other suitable enrichment
notIdealFor: People seeking a low-maintenance coat
Households unable to provide secure exercise areas or careful outdoor management
Owners expecting consistently immediate obedience around moving animals
People who cannot budget time for grooming and routine veterinary care

funFacts: The Afghan Hound is classified by the FCI among long-haired or fringed sighthounds.
The long, silky topknot is one of the breed's most recognisable features.
A shorter-haired saddle on the back is a characteristic feature of the mature coat.
The breed's history is associated with Afghanistan, while Britain played a major role in establishing the modern pedigree show breed.
Its flowing coat can make the dog appear heavier than its athletic frame suggests.

faq.question: Are Afghan Hounds easy to train?
faq.answer: They can learn well with patient, reward-based training, but their independent nature and interest in moving animals may make reliable responses difficult in distracting environments. Secure management remains important.

faq.question: How much grooming does an Afghan Hound need?
faq.answer: A great deal compared with most breeds. The long coat needs thorough, regular brushing and periodic bathing to prevent tangles and mats. The exact routine depends on coat condition and lifestyle.

faq.question: Can an Afghan Hound live in an apartment?
faq.answer: It depends on the individual dog and the owner's ability to provide enough exercise, enrichment and grooming. Apartment suitability is not recorded as a universal yes or no for this breed.

faq.question: Can Afghan Hounds be let off lead?
faq.answer: Only in an appropriately secure area unless the situation has been carefully assessed. Their sighthound heritage can prompt them to chase animals, and recall may not be reliable around strong distractions.

faq.question: What health tests should I ask a breeder about?
faq.answer: Ask about hip evaluation, an ophthalmologist evaluation and thyroid evaluation, which are listed in breed-club screening recommendations. A veterinarian can explain what each result means for an individual dog.

faq.question: What is the Afghan Hound's life expectancy?
faq.answer: The AKC breed profile gives a life expectancy of 12–18 years. Individual lifespan varies with genetics, health, care and circumstances.
